corrected_content.problem:
Which expression is the unsimplified cofactor expansion along the $3$rd column? Retain a term for each nonzero entry of that column, with the sign supplied by $(-1)^{i+j}$, even if a minor has determinant $0$.

$$
\displaystyle \begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & \sqrt{2} & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 5 & \sqrt{3} & 1\end{vmatrix}
$$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$\begin{aligned}\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & {\color{red}0} & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & {\color{red}\sqrt{2}} & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & {\color{red}0} & -1 \\ -2 & 5 & {\color{red}\sqrt{3}} & 1\end{vmatrix} & ={\color{red}0}\cdot {\color{black}{C}_{13}}+{\color{red}\sqrt{2}}\cdot {\color{blue}{C}_{23}}+{\color{red}0}\cdot {\color{black}{C}_{33}}+{\color{red}\sqrt{3}}\cdot {\color{blue}{C}_{43}} \\  & ={\color{red}\sqrt{2}}\cdot {\color{blue}(-1)^{2+3}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 5 & 1\end{vmatrix}}+{\color{red}\sqrt{3}}\cdot {\color{blue}(-1)^{4+3}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{vmatrix}} \\  & =-\sqrt{2}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 5 & 1\end{vmatrix}-\sqrt{3}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}$$
